thread:
maria_support: Hey team, acme-corp reached out — their private VPC started getting NXDOMAIN for api.acme.internal yesterday evening. They say it was working for weeks then flipped. No prod deploys on our side. Can someone grab a quick debug?

sam_sre: On it. Do we have a repro VPC + example from the customer?

customer_jane: @maria_support sending details: VPC vpc-0a1b2c3d in account 123456789012, nodes in private subnets. DNS queries to api.prod.acme.internal return NXDOMAIN from apps but curl to the public health check works. I gave a dig output below.

customer_jane: ```
$ dig api.prod.acme.internal @10.0.0.2 +short
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345

```

leo_neteng: Quick sanity: is 10.0.0.2 their resolver IP? Could be VPC resolv or a forwarder. Ask for /etc/resolv.conf and any resolver rules.

maria_support: They attached /etc/resolv.conf: `search acme.internal` and `nameserver 10.0.0.2`. No `options` weirdness.

sam_sre: I'll ask them to tcpdump on one node to see where the query goes and whether a response comes back. Also check AWS Route53 private hosted zones and VPC associations from our side (the model endpoint is in our shared service account).

customer_jane: tcpdump attached: ```
$ sudo tcpdump -n -s0 -vvv udp port 53
12:01:02.123456 IP 10.0.1.12.54000 > 10.0.0.2.53: 12345+ A? api.prod.acme.internal. (45)
12:01:02.123498 IP 10.0.0.2.53 > 10.0.1.12.54000: 12345 NXDomain 0/1/0 (78)
```

leo_neteng: NXDomain coming from their configured resolver (10.0.0.2). Two likely causes: (1) the hosted zone that should answer is not associated with that VPC (so resolver forwards to corporate forwarder that doesn't know the private records), or (2) there's a forwarding rule (Route53 Resolver Rule) pointing queries for `prod.acme.internal` to a corporate DNS appliance that returns NXDOMAIN.

sam_sre: I've checked our side: our private hosted zone `prod.acme.internal` exists in account 999888777 and is associated with our service VPCs and the shared-services VPC where endpoints live. But the customer's VPC (account 123456789012) does not appear in the hosted zone associations.

maria_support: So the customer expects cross-account resolution to work? They said it worked previously. Could something have changed on their side (VPC detach/assoc, resolver rule change)?

customer_jane: We did a network re-org last week, moved some nodes between subnets and attached a new on-prem VPN. We also added a Route53 Resolver outbound endpoint and a rule to forward `*.acme.internal` to corp-dns 10.10.10.5.

leo_neteng: That rings true — forwarding to corp-dns will override return values. If the corporate DNS doesn't have the private hosted zone records, you'll get NXDOMAIN. Also if the cross-account hosted zone was never associated with their VPC, previously they may have been resolving via shared VPC peering or an older resolver rule.

sam_sre: Can you run this from a node and paste output?

customer_jane: ```
$ dig api.prod.acme.internal @10.10.10.5 +tcp +short
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 67890

$ dig api.prod.acme.internal @10.0.0.2 +short
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 54321
```

maria_support: So both the corp forwarder and the local resolver say NXDOMAIN. That matches the tcpdump.

leo_neteng: Action plan: 1) verify which hosted zone holds the records; 2) verify VPC associations for that hosted zone; 3) check Route53 Resolver rules (in their account) for forwarders that would capture `prod.acme.internal`; 4) temporary workaround: add a conditional forwarder or associate the hosted zone with their VPC.

sam_sre: I looked up the hosted zone: it's in our account 999888777 as `Z-PRIVATE-PROD`. It has the A records for api.prod.acme.internal. That zone is associated with our service VPCs but not with the customer's VPC. So the customer's resolver never reaches it. 

maria_support: Why did this work before? Two possibilities: A) they had a peering that used to route to our VPC which was removed during re-org; B) they had no resolver forward rule previously and the default VPC DNS forwarded to a resolver that had the zone associated. Customer said they created the outbound endpoint + rule last week — that's the culprit.

customer_jane: If we associate our VPC with their hosted zone, will that work? They don't want cross-account association.

leo_neteng: Cross-account association is allowed but requires explicit association of the target VPC with the hosted zone owner. If they don't want that, they need either: - remove the resolver rule that forwards to corp-dns for that domain so their nodes will use VPC resolver which can be associated to the zone (but still needs association), OR - create a private hosted zone in their account and replicate the records, OR - adjust the corporate DNS to forward queries for `prod.acme.internal` to the account hosting the private zone (via resolver inbound endpoint).

sam_sre: Short-term fix we recommended: remove the `prod.acme.internal` Route53 Resolver rule that forwards to 10.10.10.5 (their corp DNS) or change its priority so it doesn't match. We asked them to try deleting the rule and retest.

customer_jane: Deleted the rule and retested: ```
$ dig api.prod.acme.internal @10.0.0.2 +short
34.201.12.99
```

maria_support: Nice — now it resolves to our service IP. Can you curl the endpoint?

customer_jane: `curl https://api.prod.acme.internal/health` -> 200 OK. All good now.

leo_neteng: Root cause summary: customer added a Route53 Resolver rule that forwarded `*.acme.internal` to a corporate forwarder which did not have the private hosted zone data, causing NXDOMAIN. Secondary factor: customer VPC was not associated with the private hosted zone in the account that owns the records, so cross-account association or replication would be required for persistent fix.

maria_support: Customer will either remove the rule permanently, replicate the private zone into their account, or request cross-account VPC association via support. I logged a ticket for cross-account association help.

deploy-bot: ticket#INC-2026-11234 created and linked to this thread.

sam_sre: Adding runbook notes: check tcpdump -> if resolver replies NXDomain, check outbound resolver rules and corp forwarders; verify VPC association list on the private zone owner account; confirm any recent VPN/VPC re-org that added forwarding. I'll update the internal KB with the exact commands we used. :memo:

maria_support: Thanks all — I'll close once customer picks a permanent option. :thumbsup:
